acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Bears family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Scrub Bear, T1, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Swipe-Commit Initiate archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Small shaggy bear with a long muzzle, uneven seasonal coat, ordinary claws, and slightly underfed flanks.
Signature mechanic: Standing Swipe: the Bear rises, loads one shoulder, and sweeps once before an unavoidable heavy landing.
battlefieldDuty: Deliver one broad forepaw swipe after standing, then drop heavily onto all fours.
constructionDimensions: Long guard hairs stream into layered directional sheets while the dense opaque body and heavy paws remain grounded.
Pressure rolls outward from swipes and roars, with leaves and dust marking the exact cone or fall lane.
counterplay: Move under the raised side and punish the landing recovery from the rear quarter. Affinity signal: The active pressure sheet collapses into a still pocket at the planted paw or open chest after release.
forbiddenTreatments: Diffuse wind that conceals the committed lane
identityInvariants: Every form retains a four-legged ursine body, plantigrade paws, compact tail, broad muzzle, dense coat, and weight-bearing shoulder hump.
Escalation uses coat condition, scars, claw specialization, posture, and environmental interaction rather than humanoid equipment.
Raised shoulders, planted hind legs, open chest, and exposed inner wrists preserve readable commitment and recovery windows.
telegraph: Its hips settle and the striking shoulder rises above the other forepaw.
